Only three sheets of newspaper were left, and the rain puddles outside would dry by evening. Urmila wanted a boat that floated.
She folded the first one tall and thin. In the bucket, it tipped over at once.
She folded the second one with a pointy front. It floated, then leaned and sank.
Her brother Suraj said, "Just give up."
Urmila looked at both soggy boats. "The thin one fell. The pointy one leaned." She folded the last sheet flat and wide at the bottom.
It sat in the water, straight and steady.
"Wide bottom," she told Suraj. "I'm always making it like this now."

qa.q: How many sheets of newspaper were left?
qa.a: Only three sheets of newspaper were left.

qa.q: How did Urmila feel when her brother said to give up?
qa.a: She felt determined, so she looked at both soggy boats to work out what went wrong instead of stopping.

qa.q: What else could Urmila try if she wants an even steadier boat?
qa.a: She could fold the wide one again with thicker paper, changing one thing at a time to see what helps.

qa.q: How might Suraj see Urmila's steady boat?
qa.a: Suraj may be surprised and a bit impressed, since he thought she should give up and she found the trick with the last sheet.

On the balcony of their Lucknow flat, Hafsa had a bucket of water and a pile of paper boats. Dhruv from next door watched.
"This one is tall," Hafsa said, and dropped it in. It fell on its side.
"This one is long." It floated, then tipped.
"This one is fat at the bottom." It floated and stayed straight, even when Dhruv blew on it.
Hafsa pointed. "Fat one wins. Fat bottom doesn't fall."
Next day, when Dhruv asked her to make him a boat, she folded the wide one straight away, without trying the others.

qa.q: What happened to the tall boat?
How did Hafsa feel when the fat boat stayed straight even when Dhruv blew on it?
qa.a: She felt proud and sure of herself, pointing and declaring that the fat one wins.

qa.q: What could Hafsa test next, now that she knows the wide base works?
qa.a: She could try different papers with the wide fold, since changing one thing at a time will show what else keeps it steady.

qa.q: How might Dhruv see Hafsa's boats the next day?
qa.a: Dhruv may be impressed that she knows exactly which boat to fold, and happy to get one that floats straight.
